title: Moroccan Mint Tea with Gunpowder Green Tea
summary: Gunpowder green tea is rinsed with boiling water, then steeped for 5 minutes with fresh mint and sugar and poured from a height so it froths.
equipment: teapot or heatproof jug (at least 1.5 litres)

ingredients.note: 60 ml to rinse the leaves, 1000 ml to brew

ingredients.item: fresh spearmint leaves, plus sprigs to serve

steps.title: Rinse the tea
steps.text: Put the tea in the small bowl, pour over 60 ml of the boiling water, swirl for a few seconds and pour the water off through the sieve, keeping the leaves. This takes the edge off any bitterness.

steps.title: Brew
steps.text: Put the rinsed tea, mint and sugar in the teapot, pour in the remaining 1 litre boiling water and stir until the sugar dissolves. Cover and steep for 5 minutes, no longer.

steps.title: Pour high
steps.text: Strain into the glasses, lifting the pot high as you pour so the tea froths, then lower it before moving to the next glass.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add a fresh mint sprig to each glass and serve straight away, holding the glass by its rim as it is very hot.

tips: Spearmint is traditional; peppermint is sharper and can taste medicinal.
Steeping longer than 5 minutes makes green tea bitter.
Pouring from height cools the tea slightly and gives the prized foam.
Moroccans often serve it sweeter; add sugar to taste.
storage: Best drunk fresh. Leftover tea can be chilled for up to 1 day and served over ice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
